- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model underestimates downward momentum; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 70% recent price, 30% sentiment) to anchor forecast.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply 1–2 day lag correction to avoid premature recovery forecasts.
